profile.org_note: Flat, market-led structure: per the company's news page, each of its 19 markets is led by an area president or division president who selects preliminary sites, monitors lot completion and runs building; the only multi-market leader confirmed in 2025-2026 is Texas region president Ken McDonald (DFW and Austin), with Houston under a senior division president, and all division operations roll up to COO Ladd Fargo. Land deals originate with the division/area president and division land teams; at corporate, President and Vice Chairman Chris Weekley covers developer relationships and land, and no Chief Land Officer or corporate land/treasury head is named publicly.
profile.summary: Houston-based private builder founded in 1976, operating in 19 markets across 13 states with about 1,790 team members and nearly 300 communities; its press-kit fact sheets show roughly 5,850 closings in 2025, led by Houston (1,148), Dallas/Ft. Worth (943), Tampa (471), Jacksonville (446), Austin (393) and Phoenix (381). Ownership is unusual: per the company, about a third is held by charitable trusts and about a third by team members through an ESOP set up in 2018. It both buys finished homesites from master-plan developers (156 lots in Verona, Pasco County, from Eisenhower Property Group in July 2026) and self-develops (Starkey Ranch in Tampa and a 42-acre parcel in Gilbert, AZ in 2025), and it has a stated goal of doubling closings; a new CFO from private equity arrived in August 2026.
